workflow_hypothesis: Unescaped substitution marker breaks display rendering
pattern: Literal reserved marker in display text is misinterpreted as a formatting directive
description: An interface accepts display text containing literal caller content but later processes that text as a substitution template during rendering.
precondition: A caller supplies display text containing a reserved substitution marker without the escaping required by the formatting syntax.
critical_operation: The rendering path applies substitution expansion to the supplied display text.
interference: The reserved marker is parsed as the start of a substitution directive instead of remaining literal display content.
invalid_assumption: The implementation assumes display text is valid template text, or that callers will escape literal reserved markers themselves.
failure: Rendering raises a formatting error and fails to display the intended text.
search_strategy: Inspect display-text rendering paths for implicit formatting or substitution of caller-controlled strings.
Check whether reserved syntax characters in supplied display text are escaped before template expansion.
Trace malformed or incomplete substitution-directive errors back to the original display-text boundary.
Verify documentation and validation distinguish literal display text from substitution templates.

evidence.supports: The report shows that a literal percent marker in supplied help text is later processed by percent-style substitution, interpreted as an invalid directive, and rejected; escaping the marker produces the intended literal output.

scope_note: This is a singleton pattern, scoped to display interfaces that intentionally apply substitution formatting during rendering; it does not generalize to display paths without template interpretation.
